Contribute up to $10 million toward construction of a new NYPD substation for the 45th Precinct
Status: UNVERIFIED
Citation c1 documents the promise itself: Bally’s said, "A key component of this commitment is our up to $10 million capital contribution towards the construction of a new NYPD substation for the 45th Precinct." Citation c6 provides related proposal context that Bally’s would "host an NYPD substation within the property." But none of the provided citations directly show actual construction, actual transfer of capital funds, or an operating substation for the 45th Precinct.
Promised scope: Promisor: Bally’s. Intended beneficiaries: the NYPD 45th Precinct/public safety operations serving that precinct. Location: a new NYPD substation for the 45th Precinct; another excerpt says Bally’s would host an NYPD substation within the property. Benefit/action promised: an up to $10 million capital contribution toward construction of the new substation. Material conditions: the broader amendment materials describe support methodology as something Bally’s would explore upon awarding of a license, but the cited $10 million passage itself states the contribution commitment without a specific payment date.
Observed scope: Observed evidence shows only that Bally’s publicly proposed or agreed to this capital contribution for a 45th Precinct substation. No cited excerpt shows that construction occurred, that funds were actually contributed, or that the substation was actually built or operating at any location.
Evidence gap: Missing direct evidence of actual delivery for the promised population/scope: for example, proof that Bally’s paid some or all of the capital contribution, that construction of the new 45th Precinct substation occurred, and where/when that happened.
Promise evidence: c1, c6, c7

Provide $5 million annually for NYPD public safety staffing, support, or associated needs in conjunction with the substation
Status: UNVERIFIED
Citations c2, c4, and c5 document the promise terms: Bally’s said it would amend its commitment to provide "$5 million dollars annually for the purposes of staffing and support," confirmed that the amount was "for all NYPD associated needs in conjunction with the NYPD substation we will house," and stated that it had "agreed to dedicate $5 million annually for NYPD overtime or Paid Detail programs." Citation c3 corroborates that the Board understood Bally’s to have increased the proposed amount from $3 million to $5 million. However, these excerpts document the proposal/agreement, not actual delivery. No citation shows that any annual $5 million payment was made or that NYPD actually received funded staffing, support, overtime, or paid detail under this commitment.
Promised scope: Promisor: Bally’s. Intended beneficiaries: NYPD/public safety operations associated with the promised substation, and indirectly the surrounding public served by those operations. Location: tied to the NYPD substation Bally’s said it would house; the excerpts do not separately specify a broader geographic area beyond that context. Benefit/action promised: Bally’s amended its commitment from $3 million to $5 million annually for staffing and support; related excerpts describe this as for "all NYPD associated needs" in conjunction with the substation and for "NYPD overtime or Paid Detail programs." Material conditions: annual support, associated with the substation/public-safety commitment.
Observed scope: Observed evidence shows only that Bally’s reported agreeing to provide $5 million annually and that the Board noted Bally’s increased the proposed amount during the CAC process. No cited excerpt shows any actual annual payment, actual NYPD staffing/support funded, identified recipients, or actual availability of funded support at a specific location.
Evidence gap: Missing direct evidence of actual delivery: proof of one or more annual payments, when they were made, what NYPD support they funded, and that the promised public-safety support was actually provided in connection with the substation commitment.
Promise evidence: c2, c3, c4, c5, c7

findings.claim: In Bally’s September 2025 amendment to its RFA response, Bally’s committed to make an up to $10 million capital contribution toward construction of a new NYPD substation for the 45th Precinct.

supports.excerpt: A key component of this commitment is our up to $10 million capital contribution towards the construction of a new NYPD substation for the 45th Precinct.
supports.summary: Bally’s said a “key component” of its commitment was an “up to $10 million capital contribution” toward construction of a new NYPD substation for the 45th Precinct.
supports.explanation: This passage directly states the promisor, amount, purpose, and scope of the capital contribution for the substation.

findings.claim: In September 2025, Bally’s said it would amend an earlier Community Benefits Agreement commitment from up to $3 million annually for NYPD staffing to $5 million annually for NYPD staffing and support, after a request from the CAC.

supports.excerpt: The Board notes that Bally’s agreed to increase this amount from $3 million to $5 million during the Community Advisory Committee process.
supports.summary: The Gaming Facility Location Board later noted that Bally’s “agreed to increase this amount from $3 million to $5 million during the Community Advisory Committee process.”
supports.explanation: This independent board statement corroborates that the annual commitment was increased during the CAC process.

supports.excerpt: This was outlined in our Community Benefits Agreement, where we initially intended to fund up to $3 million dollars annually for purposes of staffing. Hearing the request from the CAC, we will amend our commitment to provide $5 million dollars annually for the purposes of staffing and support.
supports.summary: Bally’s said its Community Benefits Agreement had initially contemplated funding “up to $3 million dollars annually” for staffing, and that, after a request from the CAC, it would amend that commitment to “$5 million dollars annually for the purposes of staffing and support.”
supports.explanation: This passage documents both the original annual staffing commitment and the later amendment increasing it to $5 million annually, with the reason for the change.

findings.claim: In September 2025, Bally’s described the $5 million annual commitment as covering all NYPD-associated needs in conjunction with the NYPD substation it would house, including NYPD overtime or Paid Detail programs.

supports.excerpt: Confirming that the $5 million annually is for all NYPD associated needs in conjunction with the NYPD substation we will house.
supports.summary: Bally’s described the $5 million annual commitment as being “for all NYPD associated needs in conjunction with the NYPD substation we will house.”
supports.explanation: This passage clarifies the scope of the annual $5 million commitment by tying it to NYPD associated needs connected to the substation.

supports.excerpt: Bally’s has agreed to dedicate $5 million annually for NYPD overtime or Paid Detail programs.
supports.summary: In a CAC response memo, Bally’s said it had “agreed to dedicate $5 million annually for NYPD overtime or Paid Detail programs.”
supports.explanation: This passage provides a more specific description of one stated use of the annual $5 million commitment.

findings.claim: In September 2025, Bally’s said it would host an NYPD substation within the property.

supports.excerpt: Yes, we will host an NYPD substation within the property.
supports.summary: Bally’s said, “we will host an NYPD substation within the property.”
supports.explanation: This passage provides context that Bally’s undertaking included housing the NYPD substation on the property.

findings.claim: In September 2025, Bally’s said that, if awarded a license, it would later explore and define the methodology for providing financial support for these community-benefit-related commitments.

supports.excerpt: Upon awarding of a license we will explore and define the appropriate methodology for providing the financial support for all Community Benefit Fund and associated commitments related to the above commitments.
supports.summary: Bally’s said that only “upon awarding of a license” would it “explore and define the appropriate methodology” for providing financial support for these community-benefit-related commitments.
supports.explanation: This passage documents a limitation: the funding methodology had not yet been defined and was contingent on a license award.

findings.claim: In Bally’s June 2025 communities filing, the public safety package listed a “$10 million contribution” for constructing a new 45th Precinct substation, without the later “up to” qualifier.

supports.excerpt: NYPD Substation: $10 million contribution for new 45th Precinct substation construction

findings.claim: In the same June 2025 filing, Bally’s described the ongoing public-safety commitment broadly as continued funding for additional peace officers and NYPD support throughout the borough.

supports.excerpt: Ongoing Safety Support: Continued funding for additional peace officers and NYPD support throughout the borough

findings.claim: Bally’s grouped these public safety commitments under a category labeled “PUBLIC SAFETY IMPROVEMENTS” valued at “$10 MILLION UPFRONT + $60 MILLION NPV.”
